I have an uncle who's a Gen X guy but I haven't really had much opportunity to interact or get to know many other Gen X'ers so I admit my opinion comes from a very narrow scope.

I've noticed especially in the last few years or so that he's become much more disillusioned with life in general. He's one of those reluctant tech guys who has an iphone and ipad but doesn't have a single app on them and uses them mostly for listening to music. But when I was younger I remember seeing him full of excitement about all life had to offer but now he's become one of those guys that feels like he hasn't succeeded because he doesn't have the kind of life people are "supposed" to have at his age but he also feels like he can't connect with Millennials who, in general, seem to have a different view on what defines "success" in one's own life. I do have lots of experience with Gen Z'ers both through my work and in my family and I'm excited for them! I think the advances that will take place in the prime of their lives are almost unfathomable right now but if there was ever a generation who was born for constant change they're it. I remember reading an article quite a few years ago that explained the generational difference (at least where technology is concerned) as Gen Z being the first "native" technology generation and everyone before them is at best an "immigrant". I would guess nearly all Millennials feel at home with technology but most of them probably weren't using a mouse as a toddler. Now I have nieces and nephews who can't even speak in full sentences yet but they can turn on Mom & Dad's ipad and start playing their games without hesitation. I think "kids these days" get a broader view of the world than any who have come before them and maybe it's a bit pollyanna-ish but I can't help but believe that can only be a positive.

IMO, I think each generation is born with more capabilities than the one before it and to me that means that have more potential. And while technology has opened the way for plenty of increased "bad" information/noise out there (insert your favorite click bait site here) I think the native Gen Z kids are growing up learning to see through a lot of it. One of my favorite older Gen Z'ers is Malala Yousafzai and if she's any indication of the future then I can't wait for it.

I also think they're a generation growing up surrounded by the opportunity to personalize and customize more of their lives than ever before.
